hypothesis_or_artifact: H1 (H-ORB) closure `cost-bound` — the close-exit leg of the measured slippage band (A.3 rescue TASK 2, Amendment 26 §3, ADR-038)

evidence_summary: The close-exit 'slippage' is `abs(row.official_close_c - row.last_exit_window_close_c) / CENT` (dispersion.py:943-945). hypothesis_or_artifact: H1 (H-ORB) closure `cost-bound` — the entry leg of the deciding band against the registered Section 3 entry order type
label: DERIVED
claim_quote: **Under the MEASURED band it is 0.000000 there too**, with a pessimistic-cost mean of **−0.386004**. **The closure holds at the source study's own undecayed magnitude, which makes it stronger than expected, not weaker.**
evidence_summary: Section 3 registers the entry as a marketable limit at the boundary plus 5 bp (REGISTRATION.md:302-304), implemented as offset = boundary_c * CONFIG.entry_offset_fraction with entry_offset_fraction=0.0005 (signal.py:93-96; config.py:245) and pinned by test_the_entry_offset_floor_of_one_cent_binds_on_a_cheap_name. The band tool charges entry_slippage.append(overshoot + half) (dispersion.py:902) where half is the time-weighted quoted half spread over the whole trigger minute (dispersion.py:889-896) — an unbounded market order averaged over 60 seconds — and Section 6 slippage is charged on top of the already-capped fill (costs.py:222-226). No ADR, amendment, tool or module mentions the limit, the offset or fill probability; grep 'marketable limit' hits only signal.py:8,88, REGISTRATION.md:302, docs/STAGE_A_PROMPT.md:117, progress.md:141. If it does, cap the entry band at max(0.01, 0.0005*P) per name and carry the non-fill rate as a measured reduction in the trigger rate (needs the trade tape, finding 10). hypothesis_or_artifact: H1 (H-ORB) — the Amendment 24 §3 rescue criterion applied to a band whose shape is not the shape its threshold was derived against

evidence_summary: The threshold 0.040386 is the implied central mean at the registered 1.40 Sharpe (REGISTRATION.md:3694). The quantity compared to it is the band's WIDTH, pessimistic minus central, mixed on the stop-exit share (dispersion.py:954-961). The registered Section 6 band has a pessimistic end exactly 2x its central end on every leg — entry 0.020/0.040, stop 0.040/0.080, close 0.010/0.020 (REGISTRATION.md:388-392; config.py:252-254), restated unmoved at REGISTRATION.md:4055-4056. hypothesis_or_artifact: H1 (H-ORB) — the sampling precision of the three deciding percentiles and their n against the registration's own independence unit
label: DERIVED
claim_quote: > **Pessimistic-cost mean −0.426679. E2 0.000000. JOINT 0.000000. Minimum n jointly: unreachable at any sample size, at every assumption.**
evidence_summary: The deciding band is three sample medians and three sample p90s taken once, with n = 550 entry / 210 stop / 340 close over sessions_used 28, name_sessions_evaluated 560, tickers_with_bars 199 (42 pulled, 28 evaluable). The registration fixes the independent unit for exactly this reason: E2 is computed 'by permutation on session labels with trades clustered by session date, so that a single strong session cannot masquerade as many independent observations' (REGISTRATION.md:448-451; reports/stage_a2/power.md:88-89). Quoted spreads are a same-day market-wide quantity of the kind that rule is written against. No interval, standard error, bootstrap or sensitivity is attached to any of the six band ends in task2_slippage_band.json, task3_rescue_verdict.json, ADR-038, Amendment 26 or progress.md Entry 35, and the per-trade distributions are not published (only mean, median and p90), so no reader can construct one. The repository applies the missing discipline elsewhere (rule of three 3/560 at progress.md:3223-3224; an unreached ceiling recorded as absent at progress.md:1782-1785).
recomputation: Mean cluster size n/28 = 19.64 (entry), 7.50 (stop), 12.14 (close); with deff = 1 + (m-1)rho, at an illustrative rho = 0.3 the entry leg's effective n falls from 550 to 83 and at rho = 1 to 28 (rho is not measured and no value is claimed). Binomial order-statistic 95 percent intervals for a population p90: at the published n, entry spans sample percentiles 0.875-0.924, stop 0.857-0.938, close 0.868-0.929; treating the 28 session-days as the unit — the same clustering E2's own permutation uses — the interval spans 0.786-1.000, i.e. the deciding p90 is not statistically distinguishable from the sample maximum, the statistic ADR-038 explicitly rejected as 'one session's news gap'. Materiality stated plainly: this does not flip the closure — an 11.57x reduction in the shift is needed and no plausible interval on a p90 from 28 clusters spans that.
would_resolve: Publish the three per-trade slippage distributions, or a cluster bootstrap over the 28 session dates, with a 95 percent interval on each band end, and re-evaluate the Amendment 24 criterion at the favourable end; state the session count in the same sentence as the percentile, on the terms standing rule 13 attaches an n; and/or re-measure the band on the post-holdout sessions accrued since 2026-08-28, which the registration says grow with real time and which cost 0 dollars.

hypothesis_or_artifact: H1 (H-ORB) — every deciding figure measured on a selection whose relative-volume extremity is not the registered selection's, with the sampling caveat applied to one column and withheld from the rest
label: DERIVED
claim_quote: **The 5, 10 and 20 USD rows are not affected**: all three fill 20 names on all 28 sessions **within the sample**, which is a sufficient condition, not a necessary one.
evidence_summary: Every figure the closure rests on — dispersion 2.029585 (n=550), stop-exit share 0.381818 (n=550), trigger rate 0.982143 (n=560), 19.642857 trades/session and all six band ends (n=550/210/340) — comes from a top-20 selection drawn from a 200-name systematic sample of a 5,317-name listing, every 26th ticker (REGISTRATION.md:2570-2571, 3906-3907), taken in code as select(candidates)[: CONFIG.max_concurrent_positions] (dispersion.py:544). The registration's own hypothesis is that the selection does the work: the plain broad-universe ORB returned 3.2 percent annually at Sharpe 0.48 while the top-20-by-relative-volume restriction returned more than 1,600 percent at Sharpe 2.81, and 'The selection did almost all the work there too' (REGISTRATION.md:3548-3552). The measured extremity of the sampled selection is reported (mean relative volume 2.0652 at the registered 5 USD floor) and never compared to the registered one: top 20 of 200 is the top 10 percent of the sample, top 20 of 5,317 is the top 0.38 percent. The repository raises the 1-in-26 sampling as a caveat for exactly one column (REGISTRATION.md:3903-3904) and then explicitly clears the others in the quoted claim, while the same sampling changes the selection itself — the deciding population for the band, the dispersion and the stop share alike.
recomputation: Selection depth 20/200 = 0.100 of the sample against 20/5,317 = 0.00376 of the registered listing — a factor of 26.6 in tail depth, the repository's own '26.6 times larger' figure applied to the selection rather than the fill count. No recomputation of the band is possible without the full-universe pull the pass did not authorise. Direction of the bias is unbounded: Amendment 26 §4's own reasoning ('The selection rule and the wide-spread population are the same population') implies wider spreads and a worse cost, but the same names carry higher dispersion and the central mean is proportional to it (mu = (S/sqrt(252))*sigma/sqrt(k); verified 0.088192*2.029585/4.432031 = 0.040387 against the published 0.040386). The floor scan shows both moving together (dispersion 2.0296 -> 3.1992 while the central mean goes 0.040386 -> 0.085626), so the net direction is genuinely unknown and no document says so.
would_resolve: Attach the same caveat to every column the scan and the band share, and either bound the bias (a full-universe pull at the registered filter on a handful of sessions would price it) or record it as an unbounded scope limitation in the manner of SL-3.
